summary.headline: Dr. Lal PathLabs Q1 FY27 revenue rose 19.1% to Rs 798 crore, with EBITDA margin of 31.0%, and guidance may move toward mid-teens growth.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue of Rs 798 crore grew 19.1% YoY, described as the highest quarterly growth in four years, led by patient volume growth of 8.2% and sample volume growth of 10.7%. EBITDA rose 28.7% to Rs 247 crore (31.0% margin) and PAT rose 27.2% to Rs 170 crore. Management said the CGHS/ECHS price revision adds 2-3% to realisations, and it may be more towards mid-teens revenue growth than early teens. Management will not revise the 27-28% margin guidance until after Q2, and leans towards reinvesting any upside.

segments.name: Swasthfit (bundled wellness packages)
segments.commentary: Growing about 20% YoY, but its share of revenue is flat at about 27% because total revenue grew at a similar pace. Management expects this growth to be sustained.

segments.name: B2C vs B2B
segments.commentary: B2C is about 75% of the mix and B2B about 25%, which management considers a good balance and intends to keep.

segments.name: Genomics
segments.commentary: Contributes less than 5% of the portfolio and is not yet moving significantly; management does not disclose it separately.

segments.name: West India (Suburban)
segments.commentary: Growth is close to double digits after LIMS integration. Suburban profitability is no longer tracked separately after its voluntary liquidation and back-end merger.

segments.name: Delhi NCR
segments.commentary: Management aims to grow it at double digits, in line with or close to overall revenue, and says it is achieving this.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth now seen towards mid-teens rather than early teens for FY27, versus the earlier guidance; the Q1 beat was slightly ahead of expectations.
EBITDA margin guidance of 27-28% is unchanged for now; management will reassess after Q2 and leans towards reinvesting any upside into growth.
Patient volume growth guidance of 6-7% for FY27 is unchanged; management said Q1 came in slightly ahead and that it is too early to call the full year.
CGHS/ECHS price uplift of about 2-3% at company level is expected to flow through for at least another 2-3 quarters and to support margins for one or two more quarters.
General price increase is not planned for H1; it will be reassessed towards the end of the year based on competitor pricing and cost pressures.
Capex of about Rs 140-150 crore per year; 12-15 lab additions planned for FY27 and 3-4 radiology centres (Delhi NCR plus 1-2 pilots in Tier 2 towns).
International business is a 3-5 year project; management has not set a contribution target and says it will remain below 5% for at least the next five years.
capex_capacity: Capex guidance of about Rs 140-150 crore for the year, covering maintenance capex plus high-end radiology centres in Delhi NCR and Tier 2 North India.
Plans to add 12-15 labs in FY27, similar to last year; network addition numbers are disclosed once a year.
Plans to add 3-4 radiology centres this year, mainly Delhi NCR plus 1-2 pilots in Tier 2 towns outside Delhi NCR.
Capacity utilisation is not disclosed; management says capacity is never a constraint in pathology.
Sovaaka premium wellness centre: only the first centre is launched and is in the learning and stabilisation phase; no scale-up yet.
demand_pricing: Patient volume growth of 8.2% was spread across geographies; management said it is too early to call a sustained shift from the 5.5-6% levels of two quarters ago, because the fever season has not yet started.
CGHS/ECHS price revision is worth about 2-3% of realisations; the rest of the 10% rise in revenue per patient came from test and geography mix, per management.
Industry growth acceleration is described as structural and broad-based across geographies, with no single trigger identified yet.
Competitive intensity is seen as staying high; management sees no structural price change in recent quarters.
Gross margin is near 81%. Management says higher-realisation tests carry higher COGS, so margin is unlikely to improve significantly.
Weather in Q1 was unusual (more heat, some showers), and its effect on diagnostics volume is not yet known.
Tier 3 and below is about 39% of FY26 revenue.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the realisation growth comes from CGHS/ECHS, and will it continue for the full year?
qa_highlights.answer: CGHS/ECHS price increase adds about 2-3% at company level and should continue for at least another 2-3 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Will the guidance be upgraded from 27-28% margin and mid-teens growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth is more likely to be mid-teens than early teens; margin guidance will be reviewed after Q2, with a lean towards reinvestment.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Swasthfit growth sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Swasthfit grew about 20% in Q1 and management expects this rate to be sustained, with traction in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Neuome and international plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Neuome (30% stake, up to Rs 3.5 crore) is a diagnostic supply-chain innovation play with operational benefit, not a new business. International is a long-term project: Ghana (80% of Sunshine Healthcare, up to GHS 45.6 million) and a Dubai subsidiary, with focus on Africa, Middle East, CIS and Southeast Asia; no target set.

qa_highlights.question: How should the cash of about Rs 1,700 crore be deployed?
qa_highlights.answer: Primarily M&A to build presence in the West and South, plus high-end radiology centres as capex on top of maintenance capex.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost as a percentage of revenue fall to 16.6%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said this is a reclassification of logistics and courier costs out of manpower cost into other costs, applied like-to-like in the previous quarter too, not a structural change.
